GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: A MachineMonster port and the batch's second seam pin. Mawler.cs:29-44: three moves all pointing at one RandomBranchState 'RAND', initial state CLAW_MOVE (moveState3, the LAST declared -- another easy inversion), and three branches added with overload #5 (`MoveRepeatType, float`), so again there is no integer argument to misread: RIP_AND_TEAR/CannotRepeat/1f, ROAR/UseOnlyOnce/1f, CLAW/CannotRepeat/1f in that ADD ORDER. mawler.py:45-47 adds rip, roar, claw with the same repeat types and the default weight 1.0, and mawler.py:51 passes claw as the initial state. `py audit/tools/state_machine_probes.py mismatch` lists Mawler among the 7 EXACT matches. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py machine`, seeds b01-b03, 40 turns): identical sequences and 40/40 MonsterAi draws on both sides -- every transition goes through RAND, so the draw count is exactly the turn count.

guards.what: The three repeat rules -- CannotRepeat on RIP and CLAW, UseOnlyOnce on ROAR
guards.rationale: UseOnlyOnce blocks a branch iff the state is ANYWHERE in the log (RandomBranchState.cs:134-141), so ROAR is once per combat, and CannotRepeat blocks iff it is the LAST logged move (:142-157). The port passes MoveRepeatType.USE_ONLY_ONCE and .CANNOT_REPEAT through to the audited machinery rather than re-implementing them, so the rules themselves are monster_state_machine seed fact 2's `faithful` transliteration. Behaviour pinned by the pre-existing test/test_new_features.py::TestStateMachine::test_mawler_roar_used_at_most_once_per_combat (verified present by grep), and re-executed here by the 40-turn sequence diff, in which ROAR appears at most once.

guards.what: Add order is observable and all three weights are EQUAL, the exact configuration in which a reversed order is invisible to a distribution check
guards.rationale: Recorded deliberately: the sibling unit inklet in this batch has precisely that defect with two equal weights, and the only thing separating the two verdicts is that Mawler's order matches. Pinned by the per-draw sequence diff (not a histogram), which would disagree on the first roll if any two branches were swapped.
